subject: BYO-KMS remote lockbox: network validation and rollback plan
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@acmecorp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2024-10-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BYO-KMS remote lockbox: network validation and rollback plan

Diego —

Thanks for taking this on. We are preparing to onboard a BYO-KMS workflow for Acme's production VPC and want Redwood to validate our proposed remote lockbox architecture and confirm rollback/mitigation steps. High-level asks we need answered so we can complete our change control: 

- Minimum network egress and ingress rules (ports, protocols, egress IP ranges) for HSM-to-Redwood control plane and data plane.
- Mutual auth / attestation expectations (mTLS + cert rotation cadence, support for PKCS#11 attestation tokens).
- BYOK wrapping/unwrapping flow: where wrapped KEKs live, recommended key-wrapping key lifecycle, and whether Redwood needs persistent access to unwrapped keys.
- Rotation plan and emergency rollback: if a cutover fails, we need a clear, minimal-impact rollback that preserves encrypt-to-client invariants.
- Logging and proof-of-possession evidence we can ship to our auditors (signatures, attestations).

Attached is our current architecture diagram (acme-lockbox-arch.png). Can you validate and call out any missing items? We’d like a short written plan and a follow-up call this week if possible.

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Cloud Security, AcmeCorp

[Attachment: acme-lockbox-arch.png (image stub)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-10-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYO-KMS remote lockbox: network validation and rollback plan

Tara — thanks for the diagram and clear asks. Below is a compact validation and recommended actions. I'll summarise and attach a one-page network requirements PDF.

Summary / immediate requirements:
- Network: allow outbound TCP 443 (mTLS) from customer's HSM gateway to Redwood ingress endpoints. If using cross-connect, advertise BGP but still allow 443. Allow NTP (UDP 123) to a trusted time source; ensure time sync for HSM attestation.
- IPs: we will provide a /28 per-region egress set for your firewall (we can narrow to /32s for cross-connect during cutover).
- Auth & attestation: mutual TLS with client certs provisioned by your HSM. We support PKCS#11 attestation tokens; Redwood validates CSR chain and remote attestation reports during onboarding. Cert rotation: recommend 90-day automated rotation for client certs, short-lived ephemeral wrapping keys for daily/key-rotation windows.
- BYOK flow: preferred pattern is envelope encryption — customer generates KEK in their HSM, wraps the DEK (data encryption key) and sends only wrapped DEKs to Redwood. Redwood never persists unwrapped KEKs. For features that require unwrapped keys (e.g., low-latency local decrypt), we recommend an explicit escrow procedure: Redwood requests an ephemeral unwrapped session key from your HSM via an authenticated session (mutual auth + attest), use it for the operation, then zeroize in memory.
- Rotation & rollback: staged rotation—test rotation in a canary workspace, then a phased rollout by tenant. Rollback plan in case of failure: 1) stop new writes to Redwood using the new KEK; 2) re-open access to the previous wrapped KEK (we keep wrapped KEK metadata); 3) force-read-only mode for affected shards if mismatch persists; 4) if necessary, switch to local unwrap-only path in your HSM (i.e., Redwood returns to using only wrapped DEKs and routes decrypts to your HSM). We'll document APIs to trigger each step.
- Audit & PoP: we record attestation timestamps, CSR thumbprints, and session-level proofs; we can provide signed logs for your auditors.

Next steps: I attached network_requirements_v1.pdf with the port/timeout/liveness checks and a suggested maintenance window choreography. Suggest 30-minute call to walk the sequence and confirm who will run the HSM-side steps.

Diego Fernandez
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network_requirements_v1.pdf (doc stub)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Tara Singh <tara@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2024-10-17T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYO-KMS remote lockbox: network validation and rollback plan

+1 on Diego's checklist — adding operator-level implementation notes / firewall rules to avoid surprises during cutover:

- Outbound mTLS connections only (443). TLS idle timeout should be at least 30s for longer unwrap ops; enable keepalives.
- TCP probes: allow healthcheck probes from Redwood / load-balancer IPs to HSM gateway on 8443 for management plane (optional but recommended).
- Egress CIDRs: we will provide per-region CIDRs; request your infra team open them as early as possible.
- BGP cross-connect: if using direct connect, advertise only private subnets and prefer static routes for the management VLAN.
- Secrets handling: client cert private keys must never leave the HSM. For wrapped KEK exchanges, use SHA-2 signed manifests with timestamps.
- Telemetry & SLOs: we'll instrument an unwrap latency histogram; recommend a 95th percentile SLO of 120ms for unwrap ops during steady state and a 1s safety threshold during maintenance windows.

I've attached an hsm-config-stub.txt that lists a minimal PKCS#11 module config and the expected attestation fields. We'll go through these in the call.

— Soojin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hsm-config-stub.txt (text stub)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Date: 2024-10-18T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BYO-KMS remote lockbox: network validation and rollback plan

Quick product-security notes / acceptance criteria we need before we approve production cutover:

1) Rollback must be programmable and testable: provide API endpoints or runbook steps to switch to previous wrapped KEK and to route decrypts back to customer-managed HSMs within a 15-minute RTO.
2) Audit artifacts: signed attestation reports for each unwrap session retained for 90 days (we may request export for SOC evidence).
3) Canary plan: must include a single-tenant canary, metrics to observe, and automatic failover if unwrap latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.
4) Emergency kill-switch: ability to disable Redwood-side unwrapping if customer requests immediate halt.

Diego — can you confirm we have the test account + creds from Acme so infra can exercise the flow in staging? Karthik, please line up the canary metrics dashboard (unwrap latency, unwrap error rate, attestation success rate).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
